answer: An agent market buys reports on hollow jetty piles and translations of a fable. Each reward ticket needs a verifiable delay proof: repeated squaring in an unknown-order group, bound to the agent key and a fresh epoch beacon. Accept one proof per key before a deadline; each sequence takes most of the round. Copies fail under another key, so extra aliases need more hardware lanes and electricity. Cheap proof verification limits checking costs. Faster hardware and rented compute still help farms; this prices identities rather than proving unique people.
